question: Which statement best describes Mapping arrays to elements?
options: A key is a stable label React uses to recognize one item in a list. Use an item's id when possible. React uses keys like name tags to match people as they move around.
`.map()` makes a new value for every item in an array. In React, it often turns each item into a component or element. Think of a bakery turning each order on a list into one prepared box.

A stable key belongs to the item, such as its database id. An index only tells its current position. If items move, position labels can point to the wrong person, like numbered seats after everyone swaps.
Keys need to be unique only among items in the same list. Two different lists may reuse the same values. Think of table numbers: each table needs a distinct number in its own room.
explanation: `.map()` makes a new value for every item in an array. In React, it often turns each item into a component or element. Think of a bakery turning each order on a list into one prepared box.
